activity.title: What does a heart condition really look like? Not a chart. Not a diagram. Not text. But in 3 dimensions: structurally, spatially, physically. This weekend at Hacklytics'26, we built HeartScape, an interactive 3D engine that transforms segmented MRI data into explorable models, allowing users to visualize and compare healthy and diseased anatomy in real time. (Winning 3rd in Healthcare) None of us is from a medical background. That shaped our approach: not just asking how accurate the model is, but whether it’s intuitive. The computational pipeline: MRI segmentation → volumetric feature extraction → statistical modeling → PCA morphology → Vector Search → 3D mesh rendering → interactive visualization Seeing structures spatially and being able to play around with them really changes how you understand them as compared to raw data (see the transition in the images below). Massive shoutout to Shreya Chakraborty , Vehnil Rangaraman , and Atharv Singh for making this worth it! Huge thanks to Actian 's VectorAI DB and Sphinx for powering parts of our backend and analysis stack. Also, always a pleasure to reconnect with Ryan L. and hear his thoughtful insights! Looking forward to the next build! Devpost: https://lnkd.in/egGfkAGe Github: https://lnkd.in/e4MrFbw4 Demo: https://lnkd.in/exghAgE6 ...more ...more

We took “follow your heart” a little too literally. This year at Hacklytics, we built HeartScape — an interactive 3D platform that transforms raw cardiac MRI data into fully explorable heart models — and I'm incredibly excited to share that we won 3rd Place for Best Healthcare Hack! Understanding congenital and structural heart disease from 2D scans is challenging, even for trained professionals. HeartScape bridges that gap by converting medical imaging data into interactive 3D models that users can rotate, slice, compare, and explore in real time. Our goal was simple: make cardiac anatomy not just visible, but truly understandable. Some of the things we built: 🫀 A pipeline that converts CMR segmentation data into lightweight 3D meshes for real-time browser rendering 🧠 AI-powered “Lens” explanations that generate contextual insights when users select regions of the heart 📊 Structural similarity search using anatomically interpretable vectors with Actian VectorAI for soft condition attribution 🔥 Point-cloud deviation heatmaps and alignment workflows powered by Sphinx.AI 🌐 A Three.js web interface for interactive exploration, annotation, and comparison between healthy and diseased hearts This project pushed us far outside our comfort zones — from learning how to interpret medical datasets (HVSMR) to building 3D geometry pipelines and integrating multiple AI systems into a cohesive experience. Absolutely loved working with Vehnil Rangaraman , Soham Agarwal , and Atharv Singh , as well as the incredible mentors and sponsors we collaborated with. This was genuinely one of the most enriching 36 hours of my life. Check out our Devpost: https://lnkd.in/eTmyxrru Explore our Github repo: https://lnkd.in/eHV-7BMR ...more

This summer, I gave cloud computing a medical degree. Just wrapped up an incredible summer internship at Amazon Web Services (AWS) , where I worked on the Health AI organization to build production-grade infrastructure at the intersection of cloud computing, generative AI, and healthcare. 🔧 Over the course of 12 weeks, I architected and developed a high-impact AI system designed to improve clinical workflows and reduce the burden of chart review for healthcare providers — helping save valuable time (and money!) in the process. 💡 I got to work across the AWS ecosystem, using services like Lambda, DynamoDB, IAM, and CloudWatch to build out secure, scalable, production-grade infrastructure. Along the way, I: - Designed and implemented a RESTful API layer and retrieval pipeline capable of handling 1000+ concurrent requests - Wrote extensive high-level and low-level design docs to align cross-functional stakeholders and guide long-term architecture - Navigated dozens of production-grade code reviews, shipped tens of thousands of lines of code, and prioritized compliance with healthcare privacy and security standards 🚀 A major highlight: being selected to present at Amazon’s Global AI Solutions Expo, and winning the Open Mic: AI Innovation Showcase, where I shared the real-world impact of generative AI in the clinical space with teams across Amazon. This was one of the most technically intense and rewarding experiences I’ve had, and I’m incredibly grateful to my mentors, reviewers, and teammates who pushed me to deliver work that will go live as part of AWS HealthLake’s upcoming AI product offering. A HUGE thank you to my amazing mentor Sai Venkat R. as well as the continued support from Anandkiran Gurrala , Ayush Agarwal , Sagar Ghabade, and Shaker Qawasmi . ...more

What a weekend! I'm proud to share that Shreya Chakraborty and I won 𝟮𝗻𝗱 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗲 𝗢𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗹 at Hacklytics, America's largest Data Science Hackathon!! After 36 stress-inducing hours marked by sleep deprivation (red bull gives you wings) but more importantly tons of learning, Shreya and I built thera_pixel: a gamified approach to physical therapy built with ML-based motion tracking to help patients have fun while staying on pace with their recovery. Over 50 million Americans receive physical therapy services annually, however around 70% of patients do not complete their full course of care and roughly 20% drop out within the first three visits to a physical therapist. The truth is, for the average American, PT just isn't always feasible. We wanted to tackle that lack of feasibility—whether from lifestyle conflicts, affordability, or motivation hurdles—with thera_pixel. By providing engaging, responsive screen play and real-time joint position tracking, thera_pixel helps patients escape the repetitive, mundane nature of PT exercises with gamified feedback from the comfort of their homes. Using python libraries for computer vision and data processing, and MediaPipe (a Google ML-based library) for 3d Pose Estimation, we leveraged public datasets like the IntelliRehab DS (linked below) to power real-time feedback for common exercises. By temporally normalizing, interpolating, and averaging the data, we were able to create time series ground truths for key joint angles—so patients can track their accuracy and progress over time This was our first time working with core aspects of our project, like Computer Vision, Gamification, and real time Data Analysis and we learned a lot! We’re excited for where the future lies for thera_pixel and look forward to work with healthcare providers to bring it into real-world rehabilitation settings. Check out our project here: https://lnkd.in/gbi8m4m9 Take a look at our GitHub: https://lnkd.in/g3M3Wi4V IntelliRehab Dataset: https://lnkd.in/gQvTrDRn Huge thanks to the Hacklytics Team and my teammate Shreya! ...more ...more

After wrapping up my summer internship with Turner Construction Company , I'm incredibly grateful for an experience that challenged me, helped me grow, and strengthened my passion for creating the built environment. This summer, I had the opportunity to work on the Emory University Hospital expansion project in Atlanta. I gained experience on both the project engineering and field engineering sides of construction through helping coordinate trade partners to prepare spaces for turnover on an accelerated schedule, working alongside our team to solve problems in the field, managing punch list activities, and assisting with project closeout. I also had the opportunity to develop VDC workflows to improve project communication and coordination between trade partners, designers, and owners at my project and others across the Atlanta BU. Having the opportunity to experience both the engineering and field sides of the project gave me a much broader perspective on how successful projects are delivered. Most importantly, this internship reminded me that great projects are built by great people. A huge thank you to Rob Miles , my Project Engineer, for being an incredible mentor. I really appreciated how intentional you were about understanding my strengths, helping me think through my future, and always providing constructive feedback that challenged me to grow. Thank you to Arya Desai , my Field Engineer and friend from Georgia Institute of Technology , for trusting me with impactful responsibility, answering all my questions, and making every day enjoyable. Thank you to our General Superintendent, Chad Monroe, for your leadership and for creating a project culture centered on teamwork, safety, learning, and continuous improvement. A special thank you to Kayt Dayton from Beck for your collaboration out in the field almost every day. Working alongside a supportive and engaged design team was a highlight of the summer and is something we don't take for granted. We even got to play doctor and patient for the marketing photos before the ribbon cutting! Shoutout to Daniela Quirós , my healthcare partner in crime, for making the internship even more fun and being the best teammate for our end of summer presentation. Thank you to Taylor McIntosh , Kristy Tanner, SPHR SHRM-CP , Aimée Marie Ogando Melo , Justin Gentzke, and everyone else with Turner who invested in my growth and contributed to my Turner experience this summer. Even Eric Malinowski, CHC (I gotcha this time). Finally, thank you to all of the other interns who created an amazing, supportive community. I'm grateful for everyone who took the time to teach, answer questions, and make this such a memorable experience. I'm excited to take these experiences back to Georgia Tech for my senior year and look forward to what's next! #MyTurnerJourney #OurPeopleOurStrength #TurnerConstruction #Construction #ProjectEngineering #FieldEngineering #HealthcareConstruction #CivilEngineering #GeorgiaTech #Internship
